burnerConfigurations.name: Small Simmer Burner (5,000 BTU/hr / 1.46 kW)
burnerConfigurations.typicalCookingActivity: Simmering sauces, melting chocolate, holding soup warm
burnerConfigurations.description: Lowest firing rate burner found on modern residential gas cooktops. Still produces steady thermal NOx and benzene when combustion continues unvented.

burnerConfigurations.name: Standard Medium Burner (9,000 BTU/hr / 2.64 kW)
burnerConfigurations.typicalCookingActivity: Sautéing vegetables, pan-frying eggs, boiling medium saucepan
burnerConfigurations.description: The primary everyday burner on standard residential gas ranges. Burns approximately 3.8 cubic feet of natural gas per hour.

burnerConfigurations.name: Power Boil Rapid Burner (15,000 BTU/hr / 4.40 kW)
burnerConfigurations.typicalCookingActivity: Rapid stockpot boiling, high-heat wok searing, cast iron preheat
burnerConfigurations.description: High-output primary front burner. High flame volume accelerates thermal fixation of atmospheric nitrogen (Zeldovich mechanism), producing massive NO2 plumes.

burnerConfigurations.name: Dual Burners Active (Boil + Sauté / 24,000 BTU/hr)
burnerConfigurations.typicalCookingActivity: Simultaneous pasta boiling (power burner) + protein pan-sear (medium burner)
burnerConfigurations.description: Common multi-pan dinner preparation. Cumulative thermal emissions rapidly saturate unventilated kitchens within 12 to 18 minutes.

burnerConfigurations.name: Full Holiday Cook: 4 Burners + Gas Oven (60,000 BTU/hr)
burnerConfigurations.typicalCookingActivity: Thanksgiving / Sunday feast: roasting turkey in gas oven + 4 active cooktop pots
burnerConfigurations.description: Maximum domestic combustion output. Without high-velocity external exhaust, indoor NO2 routinely surpasses 500–800 ppb, rivaling polluted freeway tunnels.

fuelSources.name: Pipeline Natural Gas (Methane CH4 + Trace BTEX Aromatics)
fuelSources.description: Pipeline natural gas contains odorants (mercaptans) and trace aromatic hydrocarbons including benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene (BTEX) that off-gas during combustion and quiescent resting.

fuelSources.name: Propane / Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG - C3H8)
fuelSources.description: Propane burns with a slightly higher adiabatic flame temperature (~1,980°C vs ~1,950°C for methane), accelerating thermal NOx formation by ~12%, but typically features lower unrefined benzene fractions.

fuelSources.name: Electric Induction / Radiant Baseline (Zero Combustion)
fuelSources.description: Electromagnetic energy directly excites ferrous cookware molecules. Zero fossil fuel combustion, zero nitrogen thermal fixation, zero benzene, zero carbon monoxide emissions.

burnerPlacement.name: Rear Burner (Direct Range Hood Capture Zone)
burnerPlacement.description: Located directly below the primary suction draft zone of overhead range hoods. Wall proximity creates a 'Coanda effect' that helps channel the thermal convective plume into the exhaust filters.

burnerPlacement.name: Front Burner (Forward Spillover Zone)
burnerPlacement.description: Standard 12" to 18" shallow range hoods fail to cover front burners. The thermal plume projects forward past the hood overhang, spilling combustion gases directly into the cook's breathing zone.

kitchenVolumes.name: Compact Studio / Small Apartment Kitchen (20 m³ / 706 ft³)
kitchenVolumes.description: Enclosed compact kitchen layout with minimal cubic volume. Combustion products reach dangerous toxic saturation thresholds in under 10 minutes.

kitchenVolumes.name: Standard Single-Family Home Kitchen (45 m³ / 1,589 ft³)
kitchenVolumes.description: Typical detached home kitchen footprint. Standard baseline volume for indoor air quality modeling.

kitchenVolumes.name: Open-Concept Great Room & Kitchen (110 m³ / 3,885 ft³)
kitchenVolumes.description: Large continuous living area. Greater air volume delays acute toxic peaks, but unvented combustion products drift throughout sleeping areas and living spaces.

buildingAirExchange.name: Energy-Tight / Passive House Construction (0.2 ACH)
buildingAirExchange.description: Super-insulated sealed building envelope with weatherstripped windows. Without active mechanical ventilation, combustion pollutants remain trapped indoors for 6 to 12 hours.

buildingAirExchange.name: Standard Modern Code-Built Home (0.5 ACH)
buildingAirExchange.description: Typical post-2000 residential residential construction with moderate natural envelope infiltration.

buildingAirExchange.name: Older / Leaky Residential Home (1.0 ACH)
buildingAirExchange.description: Pre-1980 building construction with natural envelope gaps, drafty sash windows, and higher background air turnover.

buildingAirExchange.name: Open Kitchen Window with Active Cross-Breeze (2.5 ACH)
buildingAirExchange.description: Emergency natural mitigation: open kitchen window paired with opposite room window creating rapid natural air displacement.

ventilationSystems.name: No Range Hood Installed / Hood Turned OFF
ventilationSystems.gasScrubbingRating: Zero Capture (100% of combustion gases accumulate indoors)
ventilationSystems.description: Over 60% of gas stove owners report not turning on their range hood during routine cooking. 100% of generated NO2, benzene, and ultrafine particles discharge directly into the room.

ventilationSystems.name: Ductless Recirculating Hood with Activated Carbon Filter
ventilationSystems.gasScrubbingRating: Negligible Gas Removal (Recirculates 92% of NO2 back into kitchen)
ventilationSystems.description: Ductless hoods trap visible grease droplets in mesh screens, but thin activated carbon pads are completely ineffective at capturing nitrogen dioxide gas. The fan merely blows hot NO2 back into the cook's face.

ventilationSystems.name: Standard Under-Cabinet Ducted Hood on Low (150 CFM)
ventilationSystems.description: Entry-level ducted hood operating at low fan speed to reduce acoustic motor noise. Under-powered suction allows significant thermal plume spillover.

ventilationSystems.name: High-Performance Ducted Range Hood on High (400 CFM)
ventilationSystems.description: Adequately sized exterior-vented range hood covering rear burners well. Front burner capture remains limited by canopy depth.

ventilationSystems.name: Deep-Canopy Commercial Pro Hood with Stainless Baffles (700+ CFM)
ventilationSystems.description: Full-depth 24" canopy extending past front burners, powered by a high-static-pressure centrifugal blower with commercial stainless steel baffle filters.

realWorldPresets.name: Small Apartment Pasta Boil - Unventilated
realWorldPresets.description: A 15,000 BTU burner on front grate in a 20 m³ studio apartment without an exhaust hood. NO2 spikes past 350 ppb in 25 minutes, exceeding EPA outdoor standards by 3.5x.

realWorldPresets.name: Ductless Recirculating Hood Fallacy
realWorldPresets.description: Cooking with a recirculating charcoal hood believed to purify air. The filter captures zero NO2, blasting hot combustion gas directly into the room.

realWorldPresets.name: Holiday 4-Burner Feast in Energy-Tight Home
realWorldPresets.description: 60,000 BTU full-range cooking in a sealed modern home with hood on quiet low. Massive combustion emissions overcome hood suction, elevating whole-house NO2 to 450+ ppb.

realWorldPresets.name: Rear Burner + 400 CFM Exterior Hood Best Practice
realWorldPresets.description: High-output cooking placed strategically on the rear burner under an active 400 CFM ducted exhaust. Captures over 85% of emissions, maintaining peak NO2 below 65 ppb.

realWorldPresets.name: Electric Induction Switch (Zero Combustion)
realWorldPresets.description: Transition to electric induction cooktop eliminates 100% of combustion nitrogen dioxide and benzene emissions. Only food steam and vaporized cooking oils remain.
